description: The bar charts compare the accuracy percentages of different methods on the PHEME and PolitiFact datasets. The horizontal axis represents the categories: 'Ours,' 'w/o comments,' 'w/o text,' 'w/o select,' 'w/o emotion,' and 'w/o cognition.' The vertical axis, labeled 'Accuracy (%),' uses a linear scale ranging from 75% to 95% with tick intervals of 2.5%. In the PHEME chart, the 'Ours' method achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 89.84%, followed closely by 'w/o select' at 89.80%. The 'w/o text' method shows a significant decline, reaching only 75.10%, the lowest value in the dataset. In the PolitiFact chart, the 'Ours' method again demonstrates the highest accuracy at 90.57%, while 'w/o comments' and 'w/o cognition' exhibit similar performance at 85.85% and 85.74%, respectively. The results suggest that removing text features has the most detrimental impact on accuracy, while the exclusion of comments and cognition leads to comparable performance levels across both datasets.
